<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds A100 (SM80) TP=8 skinny GEMM plans for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 decode linears. SM80 had no plans, so every decode linear used cuBLASLt, which on these shapes runs split-K plus a `splitKreduce` kernel. Follows #64482 and #59214.

The skinny GEMM did not compile on SM80: its epilogue used `cute.arch.elect_one()`, which CuTe DSL accepts only on SM90+ (`CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED_ARCH 'sm_80'`). Below SM90 this PR writes the per-warp partial from lane 0 instead (same meaning: one lane per warp writes its partial sum); SM90+ keeps `elect_one()`.

## Claims

- 1.06–3.1x over cuBLAS per projection on A100 at M = 1–16 (38 plan entries, 10 shapes).
- End to end on 8 x A100 at concurrency 1, two pairs in opposite arm orders: TPOT P50 −8.3 % and −8.6 %, P95 −6.6 % and −4.2 %, output tok/s +4.9 % and +5.6 %. At concurrency 8: within noise (table in Details).

## Validation

```
1x A100-SXM4-40GB, vLLM v0.32.0 CUDA 13 image + this branch's _skinny_gemm.py and low_latency_gemm.py
pre-commit run --files <3 changed files>                                   → passed
per-plan check (= test_qwen4_exp_sm80_selected_shapes, image has no pytest deps for main's test file):
  plan selected by qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm, cosine vs F.linear > 0.999,
  max abs error vs FP32 reference <= F.linear's                            → 38/38 passed
sweep: 270 configs per (N, K, M), CUDA graph replay (50 calls x 20 replays), hot L2 and L2-flush (weights rotated over > 160 MB)
```

Cold-L2 results (the sweep). Plans are kept only where they are at least 3 % faster in both hot and cold L2:

| GDN fused B/A | (12, 2560) | 4 | 5.52 → 2.23 | 2.47x / 2.69x |
| GDN fused B/A | (12, 2560) | 8 | 5.86 → 2.89 | 2.02x / 2.04x |
| GDN fused B/A | (12, 2560) | 16 | 6.22 → 3.94 | 1.58x / 1.55x |
| QSA QKV/gate + indexer Q/K | (2688, 2560) | 1 | 16.18 → 13.43 | 1.20x / 1.80x |
| QSA QKV/gate + indexer Q/K | (2688, 2560) | 2 | 15.62 → 14.05 | 1.11x / 1.43x |

| shared-expert gate | (1, 2560) | 16 | 4.19 → 3.39 | 1.23x / 1.22x |
| LM head | (31040, 2560) | 1 | 125.01 → 110.12 | 1.14x / 1.13x |

| LM head | (31040, 2560) | 4 | 122.25 → 115.15 | 1.06x / 1.09x |
| final HC down | (320, 10240) | 1 | 10.85 → 7.76 | 1.40x / 1.68x |
| final HC down | (320, 10240) | 2 | 12.29 → 9.62 | 1.28x / 1.54x |
| HC up | (10240, 320) | 1 | 9.50 → 7.64 | 1.24x / 1.44x |
| HC up | (10240, 320) | 2 | 9.95 → 8.02 | 1.24x / 1.48x |
| HC up | (10240, 320) | 4 | 9.99 → 8.86 | 1.13x / 1.13x |

## Details

- Shapes and points that lose or win by less than 3 % stay on cuBLAS. Examples: QKVZ and QSA at M = 16, LM head at M ≥ 8, and the shared-expert down projection (2560, 80), which has no valid config. I also dropped final HC down at M = 4: it was 1.07x / 1.18x in the sweep but 0.91x in the validation run.
- The local TP=8 shapes come from the model's projection sizes (for example, QKVZ 16384 / 8 = 2048, QSA 768 q + 768 gate + 512 replicated KV head + 640 replicated indexer Q/K = 2688).
- `elect_one()` stays on SM90+: `CuteSkinnyGemm` takes `use_elect_one`, set from `current_platform.has_device_capability(90)`, so SM90+ compiles the same epilogue as main and only SM80/SM86 use the lane-0 store. On H100, all 24 `QWEN4_EXP_SM90_GEMM_PLANS` entries give bitwise-equal output with main and time within −0.6 % to +0.4 %.
- End to end: 8 x A100-40GB, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, v0.32.0 CUDA 13 image with these two files mounted, MLPerf agentic dataset, 30 min per arm, A then B in one job. The start-up log confirms that the plans are used (`Warming up CuTeDSL compile_units=36 names=('shape-dynamic skinny GEMM',)`). 0 failed samples in every arm.

  | load (pair) | arm | TTFT P50 / P95 (ms) | TPOT P50 / P95 / P99 (ms) | output tok/s | samples |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | C1 (1: A then B) | cuBLAS (main) | 305 / 720 | 5.16 / 6.52 / 7.26 | 71.5 | 278 |
  | C1 (1: A then B) | this PR | 313 / 690 | **4.73 / 6.09 / 6.59** | 75.0 | 302 |
  | C1 (2: B then A) | cuBLAS (main) | 304 / 685 | 5.21 / 6.39 / 6.74 | 72.0 | 272 |
  | C1 (2: B then A) | this PR | 301 / 682 | **4.76 / 6.12 / 6.56** | 76.0 | 272 |
  | C8 | cuBLAS (main) | 593 / 1,102 | 8.50 / 14.25 / 18.74 | 512 | 2,226 |
  | C8 | this PR | 583 / 1,322 | 8.46 / 14.78 / 19.26 | 532 | 2,065 |

  At concurrency 1 (decode M = 4 with MTP 3), both pairs agree, in both arm orders: TPOT P50 −8.3 % / −8.6 %, P95 −6.6 % / −4.2 %, output tok/s +4.9 % / +5.6 %. At concurrency 8 the change is within run-to-run noise: decode steps there are dominated by MoE, all-reduce and many small kernels. Accuracy, paired on the turns both arms scored (the benchmark's per-turn score): C1 pair 1, 239 turns, diff −0.011 (95 % bootstrap CI [−0.060, +0.038]); C1 pair 2, 233 turns, diff −0.003 (CI [−0.051, +0.045]); C8, 1,863 turns, diff +0.005 (CI [−0.017, +0.026]). All intervals include zero; generation is sampled, so 26–36 % of turns differ between any two runs. The kernel outputs match F.linear (cosine >= 0.999997, max error not above cuBLAS's).
- CI: the new test runs only on SM80 with CuTe DSL; it skips elsewhere, like the SM90/SM100/SM121 tests in the same file.

On A100 I re-ran the 38 SM80 plan entries with this revision: all match `F.linear` (cosine ≥ 0.999997, max error not above cuBLAS's), with the same speedups as before.

@@ -1104,6 +1111,29 @@ def test_maybe_use_skinny_gemm(

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k,num_tokens,config", QWEN4_EXP_SM80_CASES)
+def test_qwen4_exp_sm80_selected_shapes(
+    n: int,
+    k: int,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    config: SkinnyGemmConfig,
+) -> None:
+    _require_capability_and_cute((8, 0))
+    torch.manual_seed(42 + num_tokens)
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    weight = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    selected = qwen4_exp_gemm.QWEN4_EXP_SM80_GEMM_PLANS[(n, k)][num_tokens]
+    assert selected == config
+    output = qwen4_exp_gemm._qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm(x, weight)
+
+    reference = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight)
+    cosine = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(
+        output.float().flatten(), reference.float().flatten(), dim=0
+    ).item()
+    assert cosine > 0.999

inline_comments.body:
Good point. I changed it in b26ff89ce0 so that SM90+ is not touched: `CuteSkinnyGemm` takes `use_elect_one` (default `True`), and the wrapper sets it from `current_platform.has_device_capability(90)`. SM90+ compiles the same `elect_one()` epilogue as main; only SM80/SM86 take the lane-0 store.

Measured on H100 80GB HBM3, all 24 `QWEN4_EXP_SM90_GEMM_PLANS` entries, main vs this branch (CUDA graph replay, 50 calls x 20 replays, minimum of 3 interleaved rounds):

- output bitwise equal in all 24 cases;
- time difference −0.6 % to +0.4 % (noise), for example (4096, 2560) M=1: 4.11 / 4.11 µs, (62080, 2560) M=1: 98.36 / 98.36 µs, (24, 2560) M=16: 2.30 / 2.30 µs.

On A100 I re-ran the 38 SM80 plan entries with this revision: all match `F.linear` (cosine ≥ 0.999997, max error not above cuBLAS's), with the same speedups as before.
